{{Short description|Japanese physicist}}
[[File:Tsutomu Yanagida.jpg|thumb|Tsutomu Yanagida in 2021]]
'''Tsutomu Yanagida''' is a Japanese physicist who first proposed the [[seesaw mechanism]] in 1979 and developed the model of [[leptogenesis (physics)|leptogenesis]]. The name of the seesaw mechanism was given by him in a Tokyo conference in 1981. In 1994, he predicted, together with M. Fukugita, the nonzero cosmological constant Λ = (3 ± 1 meV)<sup>4</sup> <ref>M. Fukugita and T. Yanagida, ''Model for the cosmological constant'', Preprint of Yukawa Institute Kypto, YITP/K-1098 (February 1994); ''How do we understand a small cosmological constant'', in Proceedings of International Conference on Nonlinear Dynamics, Chaotic and Complex Systems, (November 1995, Tokyo) 127-131.</ref> four years prior to the observation<ref>For information about the cosmological constant please see [[Cosmological constant|this page]].</ref> in order to resolve the age discrepancy between the Universe and some old stars.

Tsutomu Yanagida received a PhD in physics at [[Hiroshima University]] in 1977.<ref>[https://www.awhamburg.de/en/research/working-groups/member-details/prof.-dr.-tsutomu-yanagida.html Short description] at  Academy of Sciences and Humanities in Hamburg</ref> In 1979, he proposed the [[seesaw mechanism]], that explains the mass of [[neutrino]]s by introducing heavy right-handed neutrinos. Together with M. Fukugita, he developed the model of leptogenesis that traces the [[baryon asymmetry]] back to a [[lepton]] asymmetry. Till 2019 he was professor at Kavli Institute for Physics and Mathematics of the Universe at [[Tokio University|Tokyo University]]. Some of his students in Tokyo were [[Yasunori Nomura]], Junji Hisano, and Takeo Moroi.<ref>[https://academictree.org/physics/peopleinfo.php?pid=176564 students] at academictree.org</ref> In 2019, he was appointed professor at [[Shanghai Jiao Tong University]].<ref>[http://en.sjtu.edu.cn/news/tsung-dao-lee-frontier-lecture-prof-tsutomu-yanagidas-appointment-ceremony/ report] of appointment</ref> His research includes theoretical [[particle physics]], [[string theory]] and [[cosmology]]. Yanagida works on [[super symmetry]], [[inflation (cosmology)|inflation]] and the baryon asymmetry. He is a corresponding member of the  Academy of Sciences and Humanities in Hamburg.<ref>[https://www.awhamburg.de/akademie/mitglieder/korrespondierende-mitglieder.html Corresponding member] at  Academy of Sciences and Humanities in Hamburg</ref> In 2017 he visited the Higgs Centre of Theoretical Physics at [[Edinburgh University]] as a guest scientist.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-05-29 |title=Tsutomu YANAGIDA - Higgs Centre for Theoretical Physics |url=https://higgs.ph.ed.ac.uk/people/yanagida-tsutomu-t/ |access-date=2026-10-09 |website=The Higgs Centre for Theoretical Physics |language=en}}</ref>

== Honours ==

* 2020: The Particle Physics Medal (Physical Society of Japan)
*2014: Helmholtz International Fellow Award<ref>[https://www.helmholtz.de/en/current_topics/current_calls_for_applications/article/artikeldetail/helmholtz_international_fellow_award/ appointment] Helmholtz society</ref>
*2012: Youji Totsuka Prize
*2011: Hertz Lecture<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hertz Lectures |url=https://www.desy.de/news/lecture_series/hertz_lectures/index_eng.html |access-date=2026-10-09 |website=www.desy.de |language=en}}</ref> at [[DESY]] Hamburg
*2003: [[Alexander von Humboldt Prize]]
*1992: [[Nishina Memorial Prize]]
*1989: Yukawa Memorial Prize
